original_question: Is it consistent that the dominating number d equals ℵ1 and that every 2-coloring of d×ω has a monochromatic rectangle A×B with |A| = d and |B| = ω, that is, \( inom{d}{\omega} 	o  inom{d}{\omega}^{1,1}_2\)?
target_in_paper: Section 3, Problem 3.6 (Polarized partition relations at the first infinite cardinal).
correct_elements: Your draft is already very close to the paper’s exact target. It correctly identifies the relevant cardinal invariant as the dominating number 𝔡, fixes the intended value 𝔡 = ℵ1, uses the 2-color strong polarized relation at the pair (𝔡, ω), and correctly expands the arrow notation into the existence of a monochromatic rectangle A × B with |A| = 𝔡 and |B| = ω.
missing_details: State explicitly that this is a consistency question over ZFC: the paper asks whether it is consistent that these two assertions hold together.
Define 𝔡 for stand-alone readability: 𝔡 is the least cardinality of a family D ⊆ ω^ω that dominates (ω^ω, ≤*) under eventual domination.
Make explicit that the coloring is a function c : 𝔡 × ω → 2.
Spell out that monochromatic means c restricted to A × B is constant.
If you want the wording to be maximally paper-faithful, note that this is posed as Problem 3.6 and is described there as parallel to Problem 3.2.
refined_question: Is it consistent with ZFC that 𝔡 = ℵ1, where 𝔡 is the dominating number (the least size of a family D ⊆ ω^ω that dominates ω^ω under eventual domination ≤*), and that for every coloring c : 𝔡 × ω → 2 there exist A ⊆ 𝔡 and B ⊆ ω with |A| = 𝔡 and |B| = ω such that c is constant on A × B?
equivalent_formulation: Equivalently, is it consistent that 𝔡 = ℵ1 and \binom{\mathfrak{d}}{\omega} \rightarrow \binom{\mathfrak{d}}{\omega}^{1,1}_2?
justification: The draft is essentially an exact paraphrase of the paper’s Problem 3.6, so the right refinement is to sharpen notation and make the statement fully self-contained, not to broaden it. Definition 1.1 in the introduction gives the precise meaning of the strong polarized relation notation, which matches your monochromatic-rectangle expansion. The surrounding paragraph in Section 3 explains why this question is singled out: the authors note that for every regular κ > ℵ1 they already know the consistency of 𝔡 = κ together with the same positive polarized relation, and then ask whether one can push this down to 𝔡 = ℵ1. The sentence immediately after Problem 3.6 says that it is parallel to Problem 3.2, confirming that your draft is targeting this exact open problem rather than a broader neighboring one.
